history.summary: Maysprings (Bukit Panjang, D23 OCR, TOP 1998, 99-yr from 1994, 636 units), 3BR 1,313 sqft at $1.48M ($1,127 psf), floor not disclosed. 306 m to Bukit Panjang DTL. Priced at the project's own recent 3BR median, so no real edge. The lease-decay exit risk and a crowded resale book offset the good carry and MRT access.
history.rating_rationale: Fairly priced, not cheap. $1,127 psf sits at Maysprings' own 24-month median for 1,270–1,410 sqft 3BRs (23 prints ranging $984–1,256; 2025 median $1,157, 2026 YTD $1,121), so the −13% gap to D23 age-adjusted peers is mostly the 67-year lease (commenced 1994), not a mispricing. For a 5–7yr hold the lease falls to ~60–62 years at exit, where CPF and financing limits shrink the buyer pool. ~25 competing units are listed now, and this exact unit has been asking $1.48M since at least 2026-07-28 without selling. REALSCORE 4.0 / 67.8% profitable on 845 resale pairs is only middling downside protection (about 1 in 3 past resales lost money). Carry is fine: 3.6% gross on 34 URA 3BR contracts. Score 766 overstates this unit because age_value and psf_value credit cheapness that is really lease decay. Worth buying only at ≤~$1.40M ($1,065 psf, low-floor print level) or if confirmed mid/high floor at this price.
red_flags: Remaining lease ~67 yrs (99-yr from Dec 1994); ~60–62 at a 5–7yr exit, where CPF/loan limits bite on buyers
~25 units listed at Maysprings (Sep 2026): exit competes with deep standing supply
Same unit on the market at $1.48M since ≥2026-07-28 (DB ids 500052413/500187912/500053127): the market isn't treating it as a bargain
Floor level not disclosed; recent low-floor 3BR prints $1,027–1,084 psf, so a low-floor unit is at or above its stack comps
REALSCORE 67.8% profitable: ~1/3 of 845 resales lost money
Reviews cite dated common areas (cracks, mould) and noisy grounds maintenance: expect rising sinking-fund calls on a 28-yr estate
catalysts: Bukit Panjang DTL 306 m; Hillion/Bukit Panjang Plaza hub
Tengah new town and JRL (Choa Chu Kang ~2.3 km) add to the regional amenity base
OCR region prior (strongest measured forward region)

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: $4,400/mo from 34 URA 3BR contracts in the last 12 months (conf 0.95), so 3.57% gross / ~2.1% net. That's realistic for a large-size OCR 3BR near the DTL. Counts as carry, not appreciation.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 3BR print median rose $902 (2021) → $936 (2022) → $1,014 (2023) → $1,127 (2024) → $1,157 (2025) and is flat to soft in 2026 at $1,121 (momentum −0.64). The 5.3% 5yr CAGR is bull-regime trailing and gets de-weighted. Going forward, lease decay from 67 to ~60 years works against it. Expect roughly 1–3%/yr price growth, below the 5.3% the ROI projections assume.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile; floor/facing/stack not disclosed in the listing. At this ask, low-floor (01–05) is roughly fair-to-full vs prints $1,027–1,084; mid/high floor (06–20) comps $1,124–1,256 would make it about 5% cheap. Confirm the floor before any offer.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Agent: project resale-to-resale 3BR medians flat 2025→2026 plus lease decay from 67→60yrs over the hold; trailing 5.3% bull-regime CAGR de-weighted
